lines.note: Jokusui is explained by nigori mizzu, turbid water. The scan has a small low stop after Nigori; it is retained even though the Japanese phrase is semantically continuous.
Jokuse is the polluted or defiled world, paraphrased as nigotta sekai. The Portuguese adjective continues on the following physical row.
Inficionado completes the alternative to mundo sujo: an infected or tainted world. This is a continuation of Giocuxe, not another entry.
Jokushu is nigori sake, cloudy sake; the Portuguese describes a particular white wine. Retain the source's beverage comparison rather than replacing it with modern terminology.
Completes the description as cloudy wine of Japan. The final place-name reads Iapão, not OCR Iapãs; its tilde belongs to the a.

runs.text: Repairo de taboas que vſauão an-

lines.note: Joodate denotes a protective wooden-board barrier. Repairo is the historical Portuguese wording; the final an- begins antigamente below.
Completes antigamente and explains that the boards were formerly used against arrows. The row belongs to the preceding defensive-equipment entry.
Joodogake is the cord of an eboshi cap, explicitly paraphrased as Yeboxino caqeuo. The Portuguese cordão com continues into the description of fastening beneath the chin.

runs.text: que ſe atão certos barretes de baixo da barba.

lines.note: Completes the cap-cord explanation: it ties certain caps beneath the chin. The printed de baixo spacing is preserved.
Joohō names established laws, paraphrased by sadamuru nori. Enlargement shows a damaged f between caroned ǒ and circumflexed ô; retain Giǒfô rather than the OCR vowel sequence.
Jofot is explained by harai nozoku, removing or shaking away. The damaged opening capital is G, not the OCR's C, and the terminal t is retained.

Mooshin wo jofot su illustrates driving out deluded or bad thoughts. The vowel in Mǒxinuo bears a caron, confirmed on the separate second pass; italic Vt introduces the example, and fo- continues fora below.
Completes the explanation as casting out bad thoughts. The upright S. is the dictionary's written-language label, not part of the italic gloss.
Joogioo denotes chapters, articles, or written points. Both marked vowels remain as printed; the Portuguese describes textual divisions rather than conduct.
Joogoo is defined here as the appointed hour of death. The final Gio- fragment starts the example continued on the next line.

runs.text: He chegada a hora da morte.

lines.note: Together with the preceding Giǒ- fragment, gôga qita forms Giǒgôga qita: the appointed time has arrived. The Portuguese explicitly interprets it as the arrival of death's hour.
Joogoo hisshi nari expresses inevitable death when its appointed time comes. The two x types in fixxi are visible; OCR fixai misidentifies the second consonant.

runs.text: morte em todo caſo ha morrer.

lines.note: Completes the statement that one must die when the hour comes. Retain the printed ha morrer without silently adding the Portuguese de that a modern reader might expect.
Joogi is a ruler or governing standard, paraphrased by sadamuru nori. The abbreviated Item introduces an additional, metaphorical sense on the next line.

runs.text: permet. Regra, ou modelo de outras couſas. Vt,

lines.note: The metaphorical sense is a rule or model for other things. Modelo is a single printed word; OCR inserted an internal space.
Shakushi wo joogi ni suru means making a ladle one's ruler or standard. The Portuguese begins explaining the deliberately unsuitable measuring instrument.

runs.text: que he torta, regra, ou medida recta, i, O

lines.note: The ladle is crooked but is being treated as a straight rule or measure. The following i introduces the moral interpretation of that comparison.

runs.text: que he torto na vida, ou cuſtumes, querer endirei

lines.note: The comparison concerns someone crooked in life or habits who wishes to put others right. Endirei continues onto the next line without a supplied hyphen.
Tar completes endireitar; encaminhar reinforces directing or guiding others. This closes the metaphor under the measuring-rule entry.
A second Joogi entry concerns a person's regular vessel, with goqi given as an equivalent. It is a separate sense from the ruler just defined.

runs.text: Certa eſcudela de pao que ordinariamẽ

lines.note: The vessel is a wooden bowl customarily used by one person. The end reads ordinariamẽ, with a faint abbreviation tilde; te follows on the next row.

runs.text: te ſerue a hum pera comer o arroz.

lines.note: Completes ordinariamente and specifies eating rice from the bowl. This is habitual personal use, not a general definition of every wooden vessel.

runs.text: Vara de medir terras, ou chão pe-

lines.note: Joo jaku is a measuring rod for land or building ground. The printed space in the headword and the division pe- / ra are retained.
Ra completes pera, and casas specifies house sites. The short continuation closes the land-measurement entry.
Giojrogonomi refers the reader to Gio above. The printed j is preserved rather than normalized to i; the subsequent example uses the separated wording Gio irogonomi.
The additional gloss describes public women or female entertainers/dancers. The terminal Vt is visible and introduces the following Japanese example; it was omitted by OCR.
The example concerns setting the women in an ordered row, as the Portuguese below confirms. Nami is the preferred reading of the abraded middle word; Zon. is retained as an unexpanded citation label.

runs.text: Tendo poſtas, & aſſentadas por ordem muitas

lines.note: The translation says that many women have been placed and seated in order. The visible word is aſſentadas, not OCR aſtentadas; this supports the positioning sense of suyete above.
Completes the translation with the dictionary's description of the women as lascivious. This wording belongs to the source's gloss, not an added characterization.

runs.text: Eſpaço, ou medida de Tatami & meo.

lines.note: Jooma denotes a space or measure of one and a half tatami. Tatami is a Japanese term embedded within the Portuguese explanation, not another headword.
Joo myoo is an allotted lifetime, explicitly paraphrased as sadamatta inochi. The Portuguese determinada is divided after determi-.

runs.text: nada que hum homem ordinaria mente viue.

lines.note: Completes the definition as the span a person ordinarily lives. The printed spacing ordinaria mente is retained rather than silently joined.
The example says that an allotted human lifetime is sixty years. Giǒmiǒ replaces OCR Gibmiǒ; the damaged but identifiable nari closes the Japanese statement.

runs.text: deter minada do homem he de ſeſenta annos.

lines.note: The Portuguese translates the example as a determined lifetime of sixty years. Retain the conspicuous internal spacing in deter minada and the single-s spelling ſeſenta.
Joomoku means articles or written points, with cajoo as a Japanese equivalent. The Portuguese apontamentos continues after aponta-.
Completes the definition of written points and begins an example with the divided Giǒmo-. The compressed queſe and the tilde placement in daõ remain as printed.
Moku wo motte yuu completes the Japanese example: speaking by presenting written articles. The Portuguese translation continues on the next row.
Capitulos eſcritos completes the explanation of presenting written points. This closes the first, long-vowel Joomoku entry.
Jomoku is a separate, unmarked-vowel headword about elevation in rank. The damaged m is recoverable from its strokes and the repeated form on the following row, rather than OCR Giouocu.
Jomoku ni ninzuru illustrates appointment into elevated rank. The Portuguese begins admitting someone to the number of those who receive such advancement.

runs.text: ro dos que ſobem a dignidade.

lines.note: Completes numero and describes those who rise to dignity or office. This belongs to Jomoku, not the preceding written-articles entry.
Joonichi is an appointed day, paraphrased by sadamatta hi. The headword's faint caron and the doubled t in Sadamatta are retained from the scan; its example continues in column 2.
Joonichi wo sasu continues the final entry of column 1: fixing or designating an appointed day. Its paragraph sign belongs to the example, not to a new headword.

runs.text: dia certo pera fazer algũa couſa.

lines.note: Completes the translation: determining a particular day on which to do something. This indented row is still part of the Joonichi example.
Joonoo is followed by the preferred alternative Joonoowo, introduced by italic Melius. The gloss describes a particular form of arrowhead; OCR Melis dropped the u.
Completes the arrowhead definition by specifying the head or point of the arrow's iron. Preserve the closely set doferro and defrechas as supplied by the print.

runs.text: Giôqiǒ. Comayacani cǒbaxij. i, Yoi niuoi.

lines.note: Jookyoo concerns a fine fragrance, paraphrased as komayaka ni koobashii and yoi nioi. Both Japanese explanations belong to this headword rather than to the Portuguese apparatus.
Bom cheiro supplies the short gloss; the example begins with fragrance spreading profusely. The Japanese example is roman and the Portuguese phrase italic.
The example continues that the scent is already strong. Portuguese espa- begins the description of the good scent spreading through the surroundings.

runs.text: lhãdoſe tudo recẽde, & eſta cheo de bõ cheiro.

lines.note: Completes espalhandoſe: everything is fragrant and full of the good smell. Retain the printed abbreviating tildes in recẽde and bõ rather than expanding them.
Jooroku denotes a fixed six-shaku measure, paraphrased by sadamatta rokushaku. The a in rocuxacu is abraded but identifiable in context and residual ink; it is not a word boundary.

runs.text: minada medida de ſeis palmos de Iapão.

lines.note: Completes determinada and describes a measure of six Japanese palmos. The translation is the dictionary's own unit comparison, not a modern conversion.
A separate Jooroku, with circumflexed ô, means sixes on dice. It must not be merged with the preceding measurement entry, whose vowel mark differs.

Joosaku is a fixed method of making something, paraphrased as sadamatta tsukuri. The preferred Giǒſacu retains a very weak trace above o as a caron; the supplied NINJAL index supports the lexical identification, but the local accent remains faint. The double t in Sadamatta is visible.
Completes the definition as a particular way of making the thing. This short row belongs to Giǒſacu, not to the following flight/dispersal entry.
Joosan is glossed as nige chiru, fleeing and scattering. Portuguese fugir espalhandoſe matches the combined motion and dispersal sense.
The gloss adds disappearing or absconding, with servants and farmers as examples. Deſaparecer is one word; the OCR's internal space is unsupported.
Jotei is a queen, with kisaki as the Japanese equivalent. The conspicuous initial Q belongs to Qiſaqi and is not a separate ornament.

runs.text: Giǒtô. Sadamaritaru. i, Tçuneni aru to-

lines.note: Jootoo is an enduring or regularly maintained light, paraphrased as tsune ni aru tomoshibi. The initial sadamaritaru expresses being fixed or established; tomoshibi is divided after to-.

runs.text: Lampada que ſempre arde, ou caſ-

lines.note: Moxibi completes tomoshibi. The Portuguese identifies an always-burning lamp and begins a second comparison with a candlestick or lamp stand.

runs.text: tiçal de muitas candeas que ſempre arde diante

lines.note: Completes castiçal and describes multiple lights continually burning before religious figures. The objects before which they burn are named on the following line.
The lights burn before Fotoques or Camis, the dictionary's Portuguese-inflected forms for Buddhist figures and kami. These are Japanese-derived terms embedded in the Portuguese sentence.
Joosetsu is true or reliable news, paraphrased by makoto no soo. The headword preserves the checked final t and the synonym retains its round s.
Deiras completes verdadeiras, and certas reinforces the reliability of the news. This continuation is not the start of the following firm-heart entry.
Jooshin is a resolute heart, paraphrased by sadamatta kokoro. The Portuguese determinado is divided after deter-.
Completes the definition as determined and strong, then begins the adjectival example jooshinna hito. The example remains roman within the surrounding italic gloss.
The example is translated as a strong, constant person. This closes the resolute-heart entry rather than introducing a separate noun.
Jooshitsu is a room assigned to secluded meditation. Determinada is one word, and eſtan- continues the Portuguese construction on the next physical row.
Jooshitsu ni iru illustrates entering the meditation room. The scan supports Giǒxitni with o and a caron, not OCR Giǔxitni; the Portuguese says to enter this room.
Completes the translation as entering the room in order to meditate. The brief continuation belongs to Giǒxit and is not independently lemmatized.
Jooshu denotes a designated person who remains in attendance. Determinada is visible; the OCR's detarminada misread the vowel.
The attendant remains ready at the lord's side. Preserve the printed preſtos despite its apparent number mismatch with Peßoa; the damaged vowel is not grounds for grammatical normalization.
The next Jooshu, with circumflexed ô, denotes a count of written articles. Cajoo no kazu gives the Japanese paraphrase and distinguishes it from the attendant entry.
Completes the list as written memoranda, then begins the example with jooshu wo. The object phrase continues into motte moosu on the following row.
Motte moosu completes the Japanese example of speaking through numbered articles or memoranda. The Portuguese translation breaks apontamentos after apon-.
Tamentos completes apontamentos and qualifies them as written. This closes the article-count entry before the two distinct night entries.
Joya is the year's final night, paraphrased by yo wo nozoku and ootsugomori no koto nari. The printed compound begins with circumflexed Vô and continues across co- / to.

runs.text: A derradeira noite do mes de

lines.note: To nari completes the Japanese explanation; the Portuguese calls it the last night of the month Shiwasu. The month-name itself is divided at the physical column edge.

runs.text: uaſu que he o derradeiro mes do anno.

lines.note: Uaſu completes Xiuaſu, which the gloss identifies as the final month of the year. A separate long-night headword follows on a physical row omitted by the baseline.

A separate Jooya entry means a long night, explicitly Nagai yo. This entire physical row was missing from the OCR draft; its divided Giǒ- joins yano below and distinguishes the example from the preceding New Year's Eve entry.
Yano completes the divided Giǒyano in the restored preceding row: waking early from the sleep of the long night. Eſpertã- begins the matching Portuguese translation.

runs.text: do do ſono da noite cõprida. ¶ Item, No

lines.note: Completes the translation as awakening from a long night's sleep. The following Item introduces an additional Buddhist sense rather than another example of New Year's Eve.
In Buddhist usage, the term is explained as deep night or darkness. The scan has Buppô with a circumflex, and the terminal written-language label S. is upright.

runs.text: Officio, ou cargo ordinario que não

lines.note: Jooyaku is an ordinary or standing office or duty. The word ordinario has d, not OCR c; the sentence continues with its permanence below.
Completes the office definition by saying it does not change. This is a continuation of Giǒyacu, not a separate qualification of the following seat entry.
Jooza is an assigned place or seat, paraphrased by sadamatta za. The scan supports the first a of Sadamatta, not the OCR's u.
Determinado completes the definition as a fixed or assigned seat. The short row closes Giǒza.

runs.text: Hũa ſalſeirinha de cobre em que as

lines.note: Joozu is a small copper dish or container. The Portuguese vessel-name reads ſalſeirinha, with weak early letters, rather than OCR filſeirinha; its use is specified below.

runs.text: molheres tem a tinta com que fazem os dentes

lines.note: Women keep in this vessel the dye used to blacken their teeth. The final adjective pretos lies on the next physical row and must be restored from the misclassified bottom furniture.
Pretos completes dentes pretos: teeth made black with the dye. This is running text, not a catchword; the signature and Giǒz- on the same baseline are separate page furniture.
